paragraphs: (All pricing - Bentley W12 replacement is a high-end specialist undertaking. New OEM units from Bentley are listed at £57,624+. Used and reconditioned prices vary dramatically based on condition, mileage and service history. Fitted costs assume 25-35 hours at £100-£150/hr at a Bentley specialist.)

What genuinely moves the price for this engine is service history above all else - a W12 with documented cooling system maintenance and regular oil changes commands a significant premium. The specific variant matters too: early 552 hp units differ substantially from the 650 hp Speed and 740 hp Batur versions. Turbocharger condition (the engine has two), timing chain health and whether the cooling system has been addressed are the key variables. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Bentley W12 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Cooling System Failures - Plastic Fittings, Expansion Tank, Water Pump
items.whatHappens: The W12 runs hot - all that power concentrated in a compact W12 package generates serious heat. Plastic coolant fittings become brittle, expansion tanks develop hairline cracks, and water pumps wear. A sweet smell from the engine bay or a small puddle in the garage are the tell-tale signs. Ignoring coolant leaks leads to overheating, and overheating leads to very expensive problems - including stretched head bolts.
items.repairVsReplace: Catching a coolant leak early is straightforward and relatively affordable. Ignoring it can cause overheating that stretches head bolts or damages the engine. If caught before overheating, replacement of the affected components (fittings, expansion tank, water pump) is viable. If the engine has been severely overheated, a full rebuild or replacement may be required.

items.title: Ignition System Wear - 48 Spark Plugs and 12 Coils
items.whatHappens: The W12 has 12 cylinders, 12 ignition coils, and - critically - 48 spark plugs. Four per cylinder. By 60,000 miles, original spark plugs are due for replacement. Coils often follow. Symptoms include subtle misfires, slightly rough idle, or a check engine light that comes and goes.
items.repairVsReplace: This is routine maintenance, not a reason to replace the engine. However, the 48-plug count makes it an expensive service item - factor this into ownership costs.

items.title: Carbon Build-Up on Intake Valves
items.whatHappens: Like all direct-injection engines, the W12 suffers carbon deposits on intake valves, leading to misfires, rough running and check engine lights. Carbonisation can cause cylinder leakage and spark plug fouling.
items.repairVsReplace: Walnut blasting is the standard remedy - a specialist job given the W12's complexity. Not an engine-replacement issue unless ignored to the point of misfire damage.

items.title: Oil Leaks - Valve Covers and Gaskets
items.whatHappens: Bentleys using W12 engines can leak oil from valve covers or gaskets. Such leaks can result in poor oil pressure and even destruction of the engine if not handled in time.
items.repairVsReplace: Gasket replacement is labour-intensive but not engine-replacement territory. Ignoring oil leaks that lead to low oil pressure can destroy the engine.

failures.goodYearsLine: The W12 is widely regarded as remarkably robust when properly maintained - enthusiasts call it "bomb proof". It withstood potentially years of overheating in one documented case and still ran smoothly. The engine gained 34% more power and 54% more torque over its lifetime while reducing CO2 emissions by 25%. Post-2015 units with the ZF eight-speed transmission are generally considered the sweet spot for reliability and performance.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the W12
variants.intro: The W12 is a unique engine configuration - essentially two narrow-angle 15-degree VR6 engines joined together at a 72-degree angle, sharing a common crankshaft. It is 24% shorter than a conventional V12, offering better packaging. The engine code varies by generation and application. Common Bentley W12 codes include WR12, BWR, BWRA, CKHC, and CKHD. The code is stamped on the engine block - typically on a machined pad near the front or side of the engine. It also appears on the V5C registration document and can be retrieved via Bentley's VIN decoder. Key variants: - Early W12 (2003-2010): 552 hp, 479 lb-ft (650 Nm). Used in first-generation Continental GT and Flying Spur. Different ECU calibration, older turbochargers. - Mid-generation W12 (2011-2015): Progressive increases to 575-600 hp. Revised turbos, improved cooling. - W12 TSI (2015-2020): 600-626 hp, 664-900 Nm depending on application. Added port and direct injection. Used in Bentayga, updated Continental GT and Flying Spur. - W12 Speed (2019-2024): 626-650 hp, 664-900 Nm. Standard on Speed trims and Mulliner editions. - W12 Batur (2023-2024): 740 hp, 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm). The most powerful ICE ever fitted to a production Bentley. Limited to 18 examples. Why fitting the wrong variant matters: The W12 evolved significantly over 20 years. Early units (2003-2010) have different turbochargers, ECU calibrations, cooling systems and ancillaries compared to later TSI units. A replacement must match your exact year and application - a Bentayga W12 is not a direct swap for a 2005 Continental GT unit. Engine mounts, wiring looms, cooling pipes and transmission compatibility all differ.

relatives.code: The W12 was Bentley's first modern forced‑induction engine, replacing the older naturally aspirated 6.75‑litre V8 that had powered Rolls‑Royce and Bentley models since 1959. The 6.75L V8 was a pushrod design, far less powerful and efficient; the W12 represented a clean‑sheet leap in engineering.
The W12 has been replaced by the Ultra High Performance Hybrid
relatives.description: a 4.0‑litre V8 PHEV producing a combined 771 hp and 738 lb‑ft (1,000 Nm). This hybrid powertrain debuted in the Continental GT Mulliner and marks the end of the W12 era at Bentley.

relatives.code: The Volkswagen Group used versions of the W12 in the Phaeton and A8, but these are lower‑output (420-450 hp) and lack Bentley's bespoke tuning and ancillaries. The Bentley W12 was hand‑built at Crewe with unique components, including different turbos, injectors and engine management. A Phaeton W12 is not a suitable replacement for a Bentley unit.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement W12 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used W12 can make sense for lower-value Continental GT or Flying Spur examples where a £15,000+ reconditioned engine would exceed the car's value. But with used units, cooling system history and service records are everything - a W12 that has been overheated is a major gamble. Only buy a used unit with documented cooling system maintenance and full service history. View used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper W12 recon addresses the cooling system as a priority (new water pump, expansion tank, all plastic fittings), replaces all gaskets and seals (valve covers, oil cooler), inspects and refurbishes the twin turbochargers, performs a full carbon clean, and replaces all 48 spark plugs and 12 ignition coils. This is the right call for any W12 host worth more than £25,000-£30,000, or where you plan to keep the car long-term. The 12-24 month warranty is essential given the complexity. View reconditioned engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-value hosts (Bentayga Speed, Continental GT Speed, Mulliner editions) or where the original engine has matching-numbers value. An upgraded rebuild should include new timing chain components, upgraded turbocharger cores, forged pistons and a full bottom-end refresh. The W12 is not a DIY proposition - only a specialist with W12 experience should undertake this work. View rebuilt engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All our vetted UK Bentley specialists can supply and fit your W12 - nationwide delivery, 12-month warranty on reconditioned and rebuilt units, and fitting typically completed within 2-4 weeks. View supply and fit VEHICLE VALUE NOTE (mandatory): The W12 typically sits in vehicles worth £20,000-£250,000+. With a reconditioned unit at £15,000-£25,000+ plus fitting, the total cost can reach £20,000-£35,000. For a £20,000-£30,000 first-generation Continental GT, a full reconditioned replacement may represent 50-100% of the car's value - evaluate carefully. For a £50,000+ Speed or Mulliner example, replacement is usually justified. A new OEM unit at £57,624+ is only sensible for cars under warranty or where matching numbers are essential. Always get a professional inspection before committing to any replacement.

items.question: What are the most common problems with the Bentley W12 engine?
items.answer: The most common issues are cooling system leaks (plastic fittings, expansion tank, water pump) which can lead to overheating, and ignition system wear (48 spark plugs and 12 coils needing replacement by 60,000 miles). Carbon build‑up on intake valves is also common, causing misfires and rough running. Coolant leaks are the single biggest risk; ignoring them can stretch head bolts, oil leaks from valve covers and gaskets occur with age, and the W12 is considered robust if the cooling system is maintained.

items.answer: The W12 powered the Continental GT, Continental GTC (cabriolet), Flying Spur and Bentayga across multiple generations from 2003 to April 2024. The first‑gen Continental GT (2003‑2010) had 552 hp, later TSI versions (2015‑2024) produced up to 626 hp, and the Batur (2023‑2024) featured a 740 hp version, the most powerful Bentley ICE ever.

items.question: Should I buy a used, reconditioned or rebuilt W12?
items.answer: Used W12 units (£8,000-£15,000) can work for lower‑value Continental GT or Flying Spur examples, but only with full service history and documented cooling system maintenance. Reconditioned units (£15,000-£25,000+) are the best bet for most owners - they address cooling, turbos, carbon and all gaskets. Rebuilt units (£20,000-£35,000+) are for high‑value Speed or Mulliner cars where matching numbers or a full refresh is justified. A new OEM unit (£57,624+) only makes sense for cars under warranty or matching‑numbers builds, a 12-24 month warranty is essential on any reconditioned or rebuilt unit, and fitting costs are significant; factor them into the total.

items.question: How reliable is the Bentley W12 engine?
items.answer: The W12 is regarded as remarkably robust when properly maintained - enthusiasts often describe it as "bomb proof". It gained 34% more power and 54% more torque over its lifetime while reducing CO2 emissions by 25%. The engine can exceed 150,000 miles with regular maintenance, but cooling system neglect is the primary cause of major failures. Regular oil changes every 6,000-8,000 miles are critical, the cooling system must be inspected annually, and post‑2015 TSI units with the ZF eight‑speed transmission are the most desirable for reliability.
bullets: Regular oil changes every 6,000-8,000 miles are critical
The cooling system must be inspected annually
Post‑2015 TSI units with the ZF eight‑speed transmission are the most desirable for reliability

items.question: What is the difference between W12 variants (552 hp, 626 hp, 740 hp)?
items.answer: The W12 evolved through multiple generations: the original 552 hp (2003-2010), the 575-600 hp mid‑generation (2011-2015), the 600-626 hp TSI (2015-2020) with port and direct injection, the 626-650 hp Speed (2019-2024), and finally the 740 hp Batur (2023-2024) - the most powerful ICE ever fitted to a production Bentley. Each revision brought new turbos, injectors, ECU tuning and cooling. Early units have different ancillaries and are not swappable with later ones, the TSI generation added dual injection, improving cold‑start emissions, and the Batur used a unique engine map and upgraded internals for 740 hp.
